subject: Post-demo synthesis: recommended model options + request for customer prompt set and edge cases
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@clearriverhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo synthesis: recommended model options + request for customer prompt set and edge cases

Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick synthesis and proposed next steps from our end so we can move toward a short evaluation that tests model fit for your triage and note-summarization flows.

1) What we heard (short):
- Primary goal: high-precision clinical triage suggestions + concise visit summaries for downstream coding and care coordination.
- Constraints: low-latency (<400ms p95 on short queries), strict PHI handling (no persistent storage of raw inputs outside of VPC), and desire to catch rare but high-risk edge cases (e.g., suicidal ideation, allergies masked in free text).

2) Recommended model options to try (starting tiered):
- redwood-instruct-7b (quantized profile) — best balance of latency and instruction-following across shorter prompts; lower cost for scale testing.
- open-llama-13b-q4 (verified performance profile) — stronger on longer context and nuanced clinical phrasing; expect higher token cost.
- redwood-rlhf-3b — low-cost baseline for paraphrase / normalization tasks (useful as a fallback route).

I attached a short benchmark summary and a suggested 2-week eval slate that targets: precision on red-flag detection, summary F1 against your sample set, and latency/cost telemetry. Link to the public benchmark page is below.

3) Prompt set collection: request from ClearRiver (next action)
- Can you upload 20–50 de-identified example prompts covering: common triage questions, messy free-text notes (hand-typed clinician notes), and 6–10 edge-case examples (PHI-adjacent content you consider sensitive)? Please include desired outputs for 10 of the examples (what a correct summary/triage output looks like).
- If you have existing redaction rules, include them; otherwise we’ll share our minimal redaction guidance.

Deliverables we’ll provide after we get the prompt set: evaluation notebook with pass/fail guardrails, model recommendations with expected unit costs, and a short technical session to align on redaction + deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Next steps — can you: 1) drop the prompt set to the shared Drive folder below, 2) flag any regulatory constraints (retention windows, audit log needs), and 3) confirm an internal point of contact for security/IT?

Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB3_example_prompt_bank
Benchmark page: https://app.redwood.inference/benchmarks/cleariver-health-2026
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/86753

Thanks — I copied Ben (pricing / trial sizing) and Neha (security) to help scope the trial. Happy to book a technical deep-dive next week if useful.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: ri-benchmarks-summary-2026-09.pdf (summary of comparable healthcare evals)

From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@clearriverhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo synthesis: recommended model options + request for customer prompt set and edge cases

Hi Connor — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers and I'll start the upload today.

- We can provide ~35 examples initially. I’m attaching a redacted doc that has 12 examples (see attachment) — please note we redacted patient identifiers but left the clinical free text intact for fidelity.
- Redaction rules: our compliance team requires removal of direct identifiers (names, MRN, SSN) and replacement of dates with age ranges when possible; we can share the formal checklist if helpful.
- Edge cases to include: ambiguous symptoms ("dizzy" + elderly on anticoagulants), mentions of self-harm ideation in triage notes, lab values that are borderline but actionable, and allergy mentions that are buried in family history text.

Question for you: can Redwood promise that the raw prompts we upload will not be retained in any training pipelines or used to improve models outside our org? We need written confirmation for procurement.

I’m looping in Dr. Alan Reyes (our clinical lead) who will help label expected outputs for a subset.

Sophie Lang
Dir. Product, ClearRiver Health
Attachment: Clearriver_sample_prompts_redacted.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@clearriverhealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo synthesis: recommended model options + request for customer prompt set and edge cases

Thanks Sophie — that redacted doc looks good as a starting point. A couple of operational notes from pricing & trial perspective:

- Trial configuration: we suggest a 2-week dedicated eval (small Dedicated pool) so you get realistic latency numbers and per-token costing under a committed environment. If permitted, we can open a private trial (VPC) for audit/logging requirements.
- Minimum sizing: 2x A100-equivalent capacity for consistent p95 latency testing across parallel users (we can give exact CPU/GPU SKU recommendations after we see your sample throughput).
- Contractual ask: we will include a clause that customer data (samples you upload) will not be used to fine-tune or to improve Redwood's public models. Neha — can you confirm the exact wording (storage/retention + non‑training guarantee) so we can provide to Sophie and procurement?

I’ll prepare a short pricing worksheet and a draft SOW for the trial once we confirm retention terms and trial sizing.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@clearriverhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo synthesis: recommended model options + request for customer prompt set and edge cases

Hi Sophie — thanks for the upload and the head's up on redaction. Short answers from Security/Compliance:

- Non-training guarantee: Redwood will include a contractual commitment that any customer-supplied data placed into a Private or Dedicated environment will not be used for model training across Redwood's public or internal models. We will provide exact language for the SOW; procurement/legal can piggyback on that.
- Retention/audit: we can configure retention windows and detailed audit logs for all ingested prompts in Private / VPC deployments. For Hosted trials we offer stricter ephemeral handling and logs but we will need a short-term exception to retain logs for the eval telemetry — this will be spelled out in the trial SOW.
- Redaction guidance: attached is a one-page checklist (I pasted the short version below). If you can upload the sample set to the Drive link Connor sent, put a note on files that include edge cases so our evaluation team can prioritize them.

Redaction checklist (short):
- Remove direct identifiers (full names, MRNs, SSNs)
- Replace exact dates with age ranges or month/year where permissible
- Remove contact details (emails, phone numbers)
- Mask free-text tokens flagged as high-risk (e.g., account numbers)

Connor / Ben — I’ll drop a short SOW paragraph and the formal non-training clause into the HubSpot deal by EOD. Sophie — happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow if you want to finalize the sample set requirements.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
--
Related link: https://hubspot.example/deal/86753 (SOW draft pending)
